data.narrative:
Glyphic Biotechnologies, founded by Joshua Yang and Daniel Estandian, is a Series A–stage biotech company that has raised $44M to date. The valuation analysis draws on a universe of 3 public comparables (RXRX, TEM, ONT.L) and 8 private peers in the Biotech & Health sector, including Colossal Biosciences, Abridge, and Recursion Pharmaceuticals.

Only one valuation method proved applicable given data constraints. Stage-progression anchoring uses the $44M total raised as a baseline proxy and applies a 2.0x step-up multiplier typical of Series A to subsequent-stage advancement, yielding an implied valuation of $88M. Peer-median analysis could not be executed; while 8 same-sector private companies exist in the dataset, none met the threshold of three or more datapoints when filtered by stage, adjacency, or valuation tier. Public-comp anchoring using the sector's 6.6x price-to-sales median is inapplicable because Glyphic's revenue is not disclosed.

The analysis supports a valuation range of $75M (low) to $101M (high), with a median point of $88M. This range rests entirely on the stage-progression method, making it sensitive to the validity of the 2.0x multiplier assumption and the use of total raised as a valuation proxy. Key uncertainties include the absence of comparable-company revenue multiples, limited granular data on same-stage private peers, and Glyphic's own revenue or burn metrics, which would anchor downstream financing and exit scenarios more precisely.
